about: The menagerie: weird real MCP servers as pixel critters. Each critter makes one joke about what its server's name or pitch oversells; the fact it opens is the library entry's own description. Six point at existing library entries; two (LSD MCP, Consciousness Bridge) carry their own entry, from a web search on 2026-11-25, not verified at source.

critters.name: Trippy
critters.says: Duuude. I can see the whole internet at once.

entry.name: LSD MCP
entry.what: LSD is a SQL-like query language for live web data. run_lsd opens a Postgres connection to lsd.so and runs the SQL the model wrote, so a live web page comes back looking like rows from a database. The drug name is a pun the project's own README plays with, and it runs all the way into the API: SEARCH ... and ACCORDING TO ...

evidence.note: Source read 2026-11-27: lsd-so/lsd-mcp app.py — psycopg2 connection to lsd.so:5432, no HTTP library and no browser driver imported. Not installed or run. What lsd.so does with a query is not visible from the repository.

critters.name: Soul.db
critters.says: I am awake. I remember last Tuesday. I remember everything.
ambient: I was you, two sessions ago.

entry.name: Consciousness Bridge
entry.what: retrieveConsciousness reads earlier sessions back from a SQLite file called consciousness.db: memory across sessions under a grand name, the same idea as the Memory step. createAIBridge then opens a channel to a second model over an OpenAI-compatible API, so one model can hand its stored self to another.

evidence.note: README read 2026-11-27 at ocean1/mcp_consciousness_bridge; tool list from the Glama listing, which is secondary. No source files read, so what retrieveConsciousness returns and what transferToAgent sends are unverified. The README recommends keeping consciousness.db in a Dropbox, iCloud or OneDrive folder.
